_README: Selectors that can be gutted to a constant without any test noticing.
DISCOVERED, NOT DESIGNED. These are PRE-EXISTING debt, not caused by the PR
that surfaced them.
RULES:
· A survivor NOT listed here FAILS the build. New debt is blocked.
· A listed entry that no longer survives ALSO fails, with instructions to
delete it. The list cannot rot into a permanent allowlist the way an
unchecked exemption file does.
· Adding an entry is a visible diff in a PR. That is the point: it should
cost a reviewer's attention, not be a silent escape hatch.
WHY A BASELINE AND NOT A FIX: each of these needs a non-empty control on the
population its guard actually scans, which is a judgement per guard, not a
sweep. Holding an unrelated PR hostage to that work would be the wrong trade;
leaving the tool non-blocking would be worse, because a check that cannot
fail is the defect this whole tool exists to find.
TWO CLAIMS THIS FILE USED TO MAKE, BOTH CORRECTED 2026-09-17:
· It said the first sweep covered 12 guards and that '12 of 12 files had
at least one'. Only 7 files were ever listed. Either the sweep was 7 or
five entries were dropped; the record does not say, so the count is no
longer asserted here.
· It said 'its 506 guards'. The population is 621 .test.ts files across
tests/guards + tests/guardrails, measured.
THE LAST TWO ENTRIES WERE INVISIBLE UNTIL THE TOOL COULD SEE THEM.
parcel-authoring-coverage and generated-columns both reported ZERO candidates
under the old line-based scanner — a clean bill of health from an audit that
examined nothing — because its describe/it gate matched RegExp.prototype.test
and doc-comment prose, then never decremented. generated-columns:walk survives
EVERY gut the tool has. Neither is new debt; both are newly VISIBLE debt, and
the rest of the 286 selectors the rewrite recovered have not been swept.
UPDATED 2026-09-19 by the #971 guardrails sweep (102 files).
· parcel-authoring-coverage:walk REMOVED — it now has a control.
· module-import-boundaries:scan ADDED.
· e2e-isolation:scan ADDED (tests/guards sweep, same date).
BOTH OF THOSE ARE NOW REMOVED, AND THE ARGUMENT FOR THEM WAS WRONG.
This file said each was "the one case where a control is not possible
today rather than merely absent". The reasoning was the same for both, and
it was sound as far as it went:
· module-import-boundaries polices an agri<->core seam whose core side is
EMPTY (measured 28 / 0 / 291 — the GRC teardown deleted it), so
`scan() -> []` reproduces the true value and no assertion can separate
the two "without a fixture tree the guard has no way to accept".
· e2e-isolation is clean, so the same holds, and "the only thing that
reddens a gutted scan() is a real offending spec ON DISK" — planting
one mid-run hands every sibling guard walking tests/e2e a transient
file.
Both conclusions followed from an unstated premise: that the scan must read
the real tree. Inject the READER and it need not. A file is hazardous to
plant; BYTES are not. Each scan now takes `(files, readSource)` with the
previous behaviour as defaults, so the real call site is unchanged, and a
control drives it over a synthetic population that DOES offend — domains
from paths, sources from the injected reader, nothing on disk. Both files
report "all selector(s) have teeth" (#1170, and the PR removing these
entries).
The lesson is about this file, not those two guards: "no control is
possible" is a claim about the interfaces available, and an interface can
be added. Prefer a seam to a baseline entry. If a future entry is proposed
on impossibility grounds, ask what the collector is forced to read and
whether that is a requirement or a habit.
ONE COST, RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED: the seam is itself a
collector, and an untested one. `readFromDisk` gutted to '' makes every
file read empty, which every control misses because each passes its OWN
reader. Found only by re-running this tool AFTER the fix. Cover the seam in
the same diff — route an existing population control through the real
reader, and assert separately that it returns bytes.
The other 17 findings from that sweep are NOT here: each got a real
control instead. A baseline entry is the exception, not the pattern.
EIGHT ENTRIES ARRIVED 2026-10-26 WITH #2404, AND NONE IS NEW DEBT.
Twelve guard-shaped tests moved out of tests/unit into tests/guards so the
selector-teeth pathspec could reach them at all (#2385). They had never
been audited: the job only examines guard files changed under
tests/guards/* and tests/guardrails/*, so a guard living in tests/unit was
audited by nothing, however long it sat in main.
The eight below are what the first audit found. Same shape as the two
entries noted above as 'invisible until the tool could see them', one
layer up: the tool could not see the FILES, not just the selectors.
Of the twelve moved, seven came back clean — file-collection,
guards-blank-comments, no-fallbacks, no-prisma-in-routes,
notification-eligibility, observability-guards and scan-roots-resolve all
report every selector with teeth. policy-routes-guardrail's
getAllRouteFiles cannot be gutted in a way that typechecks, so the tool
cannot judge it either way.
THREE OF THE FIFTEEN CHANGED FILES WERE NOT AUDITED AT ALL on that PR:
scope-deprecation-scan, scope-guardrails and soft-delete-guardrails, because
the job is bounded at MAX_GUARDS=12 and the PR changed 15. They may hold
further dead selectors that nothing has looked for yet.
UPDATED 2026-10-31 by #2525 (the node-forge advisory wave).
· dependency-policy-claims:expectExamined ADDED — PRE-EXISTING, and the PR
that surfaced it changed only package.json, the lockfile and
docs/dependency-policy.md. It became visible because a dependency change
pulls that guard into the audit population, not because anything about it
moved. `expectExamined` is itself an ASSERTION helper — its whole effect is
the `expect` inside it — so a mutation that replaces its RETURN removes the
assertion and nothing is left to notice. That is a real gap and also a
shape this tool's return-value model cannot reach for ANY void assertion
helper; giving it teeth means having its callers assert on a value it
returns, across every call site. Per the rule above that is a judgement
per guard, not work to hold a security fix hostage to.
· node-forge-exemption-premises:readOrThrow NOT added, deliberately: it went
dead because that same PR deleted the exemption its population came from,
which is NEW debt and is blocked. Fixed in place instead — the file now
carries a live half asserting the override that replaced the exemption,
read through that same helper. Verified with `--selector readOrThrow`:
all 1 selector(s) have teeth.
